title: Physical Quantities & Their Units
subtitle: SI units, derived units, and unit equivalences
note: Covers all seven SI base units, major derived units, and unit equivalences in mechanics, electromagnetism, thermodynamics, optics, and radiation.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.exp: The newton (N) is the SI derived unit of force. By Newton's second law, 1 N = 1 kg·m/s². It is named after Sir Isaac Newton.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of energy or work?
questions.exp: The joule (J) is the SI unit of energy, work, and heat. 1 J = 1 N·m = 1 kg·m²/s².

questions.q: What is the SI unit of power?
questions.exp: The watt (W) is the SI unit of power (rate of energy transfer). 1 W = 1 J/s.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of pressure?
questions.exp: The pascal (Pa) is the SI unit of pressure and mechanical stress. 1 Pa = 1 N/m².

questions.q: What is the SI unit of frequency?
questions.exp: The hertz (Hz) is the SI unit of frequency, equal to one cycle (or event) per second. It is named after physicist Heinrich Hertz.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of electric charge?
questions.exp: The coulomb (C) is the SI unit of electric charge. 1 C = 1 A·s — the charge transferred by a current of one ampere in one second.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of electric potential difference (voltage)?
questions.exp: The volt (V) is the SI unit of electric potential difference. 1 V = 1 J/C = 1 W/A.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of electrical resistance?
questions.exp: The ohm (Ω) is the SI unit of electrical resistance, named after Georg Simon Ohm. 1 Ω = 1 V/A.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of electrical capacitance?
questions.exp: The farad (F) is the SI unit of electrical capacitance. 1 F = 1 C/V. It is named after Michael Faraday.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of electrical inductance?
questions.exp: The henry (H) is the SI unit of electrical inductance. 1 H = 1 V·s/A = 1 Wb/A. It is named after Joseph Henry.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of magnetic flux?
questions.exp: The weber (Wb) is the SI unit of magnetic flux. 1 Wb = 1 V·s. A change of 1 Wb per second induces 1 V in a loop.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of magnetic flux density (the B field)?
questions.exp: The tesla (T) is the SI unit of magnetic flux density. 1 T = 1 Wb/m². It is named after Nikola Tesla.

questions.q: What is the SI base unit of luminous intensity?
questions.exp: The candela (cd) is the SI base unit of luminous intensity. It describes the power of light emitted in a specific direction.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of luminous flux?
questions.exp: The lumen (lm) is the SI unit of luminous flux — the total quantity of visible light emitted. 1 lm = 1 cd·sr.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of illuminance?
questions.exp: The lux (lx) is the SI unit of illuminance (light falling on a surface). 1 lx = 1 lm/m².

questions.q: What is the SI base unit of amount of substance?
questions.exp: The mole (mol) is the SI base unit for amount of substance. One mole contains approximately 6.022 × 10²³ elementary entities (Avogadro's number).

questions.q: What is the SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature?
questions.exp: The kelvin (K) is the SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature. Absolute zero is 0 K (equal to −273.15 °C). Note: we say 'kelvin', not 'degrees kelvin'.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of radioactivity (rate of nuclear decay)?
questions.exp: The becquerel (Bq) is the SI unit of radioactivity. 1 Bq = 1 nuclear disintegration per second. It replaced the older unit, the curie (Ci).

questions.q: What is the SI unit of absorbed radiation dose?
questions.exp: The gray (Gy) is the SI unit of absorbed radiation dose. 1 Gy = 1 J/kg of energy deposited in matter by ionizing radiation.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of equivalent (effective) radiation dose, which accounts for biological harm?
questions.exp: The sievert (Sv) is the SI unit of equivalent radiation dose. It weights absorbed dose by a radiation weighting factor to reflect biological effectiveness.

questions.q: One newton is equal to:
questions.exp: From Newton's second law F = ma: 1 N = 1 kg × 1 m/s². It is the force needed to accelerate a 1 kg mass at 1 m/s².

questions.q: One joule is equal to:
questions.exp: 1 J = 1 N·m (force times distance). Expanding: 1 J = 1 kg·m²/s².

questions.q: One pascal is equal to:
questions.exp: Pressure = Force/Area, so 1 Pa = 1 N/m². Expanding further: 1 Pa = 1 kg/(m·s²).

questions.q: One watt is equal to:
questions.exp: Power = energy per unit time, so 1 W = 1 J/s. It can also be written as 1 kg·m²/s³.

questions.q: One volt is equal to:
questions.exp: Voltage = energy per unit charge, so 1 V = 1 J/C. It can also be expressed as 1 W/A.

questions.q: Which physical quantity has SI base-unit dimensions of kg·m²/s²?
questions.exp: Energy has dimensions of kg·m²/s² — the same as joules. (Force = kg·m/s², Power = kg·m²/s³, Pressure = kg/(m·s²).)

questions.q: The SI unit of momentum is:
questions.exp: Momentum p = mv, so its unit is kg·m/s. This is equivalent to N·s (newton-seconds), since 1 N = 1 kg·m/s².

questions.q: The unit of impulse (J = F·Δt) is:
questions.exp: Impulse = Force × time = N·s. By the impulse-momentum theorem, 1 N·s = 1 kg·m/s — the change in momentum.

questions.q: The unit of torque (moment of force) is:
questions.exp: Torque is measured in newton-meters (N·m). Although it has the same dimensions as energy (joules), torque is expressed as N·m to distinguish it from work/energy.

questions.q: The SI unit of angular velocity (ω) is:
questions.exp: Angular velocity is measured in radians per second (rad/s) in SI. While Hz and rpm are also used in practice, rad/s is the standard SI unit.

questions.q: The unit of angular momentum (L = Iω) is:
questions.exp: Angular momentum has units of kg·m²/s, which is equivalent to J·s (joule-seconds) and N·m·s — all three expressions are correct.

questions.q: The unit of specific heat capacity (c) is:
questions.exp: Specific heat capacity measures energy required per unit mass per unit temperature change. Its SI unit is J/(kg·K) — joules per kilogram per kelvin.

questions.q: The unit of thermal conductivity (λ) is:
questions.exp: Thermal conductivity is measured in W/(m·K) — watts per meter per kelvin. It describes how readily a material conducts heat.

questions.q: The unit of dynamic (shear) viscosity (η) is:
questions.exp: Dynamic viscosity is measured in pascal-seconds (Pa·s), equivalent to kg/(m·s). An older CGS unit is the poise (P), where 1 Pa·s = 10 P.

questions.q: The unit of kinematic viscosity (ν = η/ρ) is:
questions.exp: Kinematic viscosity = dynamic viscosity ÷ density = (Pa·s)/(kg/m³) = m²/s. The CGS unit is the stokes (St), where 1 St = 10⁻⁴ m²/s.

questions.q: The unit of surface tension (γ) is:
questions.exp: Surface tension can be expressed as N/m (force per unit length) or J/m² (energy per unit area). These are dimensionally identical: 1 N/m = 1 J/m².

questions.q: The unit of electric field strength (E) is:
questions.exp: Electric field strength is measured in volts per meter (V/m), which is equivalent to newtons per coulomb (N/C). Both forms appear in textbooks.

questions.q: The unit of magnetic field intensity (the H field) is:
questions.exp: The H field (magnetic field intensity) is measured in A/m. This differs from the B field (magnetic flux density), which is in teslas.

questions.q: The unit of electrical conductance (the inverse of resistance) is:
questions.exp: The siemens (S) is the SI unit of electrical conductance. 1 S = 1/Ω. It was formerly called the 'mho' (ohm spelled backwards).

questions.q: What does the unit 'lux' measure?
questions.exp: Lux (lx) measures illuminance — the luminous flux received per unit area of a surface. 1 lx = 1 lm/m².

questions.q: What physical quantity does the unit 'henry' (H) measure?
questions.exp: The henry (H) measures electrical inductance. An inductor has 1 H of inductance if a current change of 1 A/s induces an EMF of 1 V.

questions.q: What is the SI unit for plane angle?
questions.exp: The radian (rad) is the SI unit of plane angle. It is defined as the angle subtended at a circle's center by an arc equal in length to the radius. 2π rad = 360°.

questions.q: What is the SI unit for solid angle?
questions.exp: The steradian (sr) is the SI unit of solid angle. A complete sphere subtends 4π steradians. 1 sr is the solid angle that cuts out an area r² on a sphere of radius r.

questions.q: The SI unit of molar concentration (molarity) is:
questions.exp: The strict SI unit of molar concentration is mol/m³, but in chemistry mol/L (= M, molar) is standard. 1 mol/L = 1000 mol/m³.

questions.q: The SI unit of density is:
questions.exp: Density = mass/volume, so the SI unit is kg/m³. The practical unit g/cm³ is also common (1 g/cm³ = 1000 kg/m³).

questions.q: 1 kilowatt-hour (kWh), the unit on electricity bills, equals:
questions.exp: 1 kWh = 1000 W × 3600 s = 3,600,000 J = 3.6 × 10⁶ J. The kilowatt-hour is a unit of energy commonly used for household electricity.

questions.q: One electron-volt (eV) is approximately equal to:
questions.exp: 1 eV = 1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. It is the kinetic energy gained by an electron accelerated through a potential difference of 1 volt. (9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg is the electron's mass; 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s is Planck's constant.)

questions.q: The unit of Planck's constant (h) is:
questions.exp: Planck's constant h has units of J·s (joule-seconds), equivalent to kg·m²/s. It relates the energy of a photon to its frequency: E = hf.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an SI base unit?
questions.exp: The newton is a derived SI unit (kg·m/s²), not a base unit. The seven SI base units are: metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole, and candela.

questions.q: The unit of electric flux (ΦE) is:
questions.exp: Electric flux is measured in V·m (volt-meters), which is equivalent to N·m²/C. It represents the total electric field passing through a surface.

questions.q: Which unit is used to measure the activity of a catalyst in SI?
questions.exp: The katal (kat) is the SI unit of catalytic activity. 1 kat = 1 mol/s — the amount of catalyst that converts 1 mole of substrate per second.
